arxiv-2002-04307.title: Demonstration of electron focusing using electronic lenses in low-dimensional system
arxiv-2002-04307.creator: Chengyu Yan, Michael Pepper, Patrick See, Ian Farrer, David Ritchie, Jonathan Griffiths
arxiv-2002-04307.description: Abstract Abstract We report an all-electric integrable electron focusing lens in n-type GaAs. It is shown that a pronounced focusing peak takes place when the focal point aligns with an on-chip detector. The intensity and full width half maximum (FWHM) of the focusing peak are associated with the collimation of injected electrons.

arxiv-2111-03202.title: Temperature-driven transition from skyrmion to bubble crystals in centrosymmetric itinerant magnets Journal: New J. Phys.
arxiv-2111-03202.creator: Satoru Hayami
arxiv-2111-03202.description: Abstract Interplay between itinerant electrons and localized spins in itinerant magnets gives rise to a variety of noncoplanar multiple- Q Q spin textures, such as the skyrmion, hedgehog, meron, and vortex. We elucidate that another type of multiple- Q Q state consisting of collinear sinusoidal waves, a magnetic bubble crystal, appears at finite temperatures in a centrosymmetric itinerant electron system.

arxiv-2304-13939.title: A One-Dimensional Symmetric Force-Based Blending Method for Atomistic-to-Continuum Coupling
arxiv-2304-13939.creator: Elaine Gorom-Alexander, Xingjie Helen Li
arxiv-2304-13939.description: Abstract Inspired by the blending method developed by [P. Seleson, S. Beneddine, and S. Prudhome, A Force-Based Coupling Scheme for Peridynamics and Classical Elasticity , (2013)] for the nonlocal-to-local coupling, we create a symmetric and consistent blended force-based Atomistic-to-Continuum (a/c) scheme for the atomistic chain in one-dimensional space.

arxiv-2305-19864.title: Designing Closed-Loop Models for Task Allocation
arxiv-2305-19864.creator: Vijay Keswani, L. Elisa Celis, Krishnaram Kenthapadi, Matthew Lease
arxiv-2305-19864.description: Abstract Automatically assigning tasks to people is challenging because human performance can vary across tasks for many reasons. This challenge is further compounded in real-life settings in which no oracle exists to assess the quality of human decisions and task assignments made.

arxiv-2411-18913.title: Planning Shorter Paths in Graphs of Convex Sets by Undistorting Parametrized Configuration Spaces
arxiv-2411-18913.creator: Shruti Garg, Thomas Cohn, Russ Tedrake
arxiv-2411-18913.description: Abstract Optimization based motion planning provides a useful modeling framework through various costs and constraints. Using Graph of Convex Sets (GCS) for trajectory optimization gives guarantees of feasibility and optimality by representing configuration space as the finite union of convex sets.

arxiv-2504-06650.title: ThoughtProbe: Classifier-Guided Thought Space Exploration Leveraging LLMs’ Intrinsic Reasoning
arxiv-2504-06650.creator: Zijian Wang, Chang Xu
arxiv-2504-06650.description: Abstract Pre-trained large language models (LLMs) have been demonstrated to possess intrinsic reasoning capabilities that can emerge naturally when expanding the response space. However, the neural representation mechanisms underlying these intrinsic capabilities and approaches for their optimal utilization remain inadequately understood.

arxiv-2508-04234.title: A machine learning approach for image classification in synthetic aperture RADAR
arxiv-2508-04234.creator: Romina Gaburro, Patrick Healy, Shraddha Naidu, Clifford Nolan
arxiv-2508-04234.description: Abstract We consider the problem in Synthetic Aperture RADAR (SAR) of identifying and classifying objects located on the ground by means of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Specifically, we adopt a single scattering approximation to classify the shape of the object using both simulated SAR data and reconstructed images from this data, and we compare the success of these approaches.

britannica-1911-gerlache-etienne-constan.description: Article 'Gerlache, Étienne Constantin, Baron de' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 11), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Belgian politician and historian, was born at Biourge, Luxemburg, on the 24th of December 1785. He studied law in Paris and practised there for some time, but settled at Liége after the establishment of the kingdom of the Netherlands.

pmc-10488899.title: Effects of Recycled Polymer on Melt Viscosity and Crystallization Temperature of Polyester Elastomer Blends
pmc-10488899.creator: Ji-Eun Lee, Jin-Woo Lee, Jae-Wang Ko, Kyung-Il Jo, Hyun-Ju Park, Ildoo Chung, Jianbo Yin
pmc-10488899.description: As the world is paying attention to the seriousness of environmental pollution, the need for a resource circulation economy is emerging due to the development of eco-friendly industrial groups. In particular, the recycling of thermoplastic elastomers without cross-link has been highlighted in the plastics field, which has rapidly developed the industry.

pmc-12412083.title: Persistent Human T‐Lymphotropic Virus Type 1 (HTLV‐1) Infection in the Placenta of Pregnant Women
pmc-12412083.creator: Gabriela Prates, Xiaoyi Li, Victor Folgosi, George Souza, Sandy Teixeira, Carlos Apoliano, Fernanda Grassi, Jacielma Freire, Jerusa Smid, Michel E Haziot, Rosa Maria N Marcusso, Augusto C P de Oliveira, Hongjie Chen, Tatiane Assone, Yuyang Tang, Guochun Jiang, Jorge Casseb
pmc-12412083.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Mother‐to‐child transmission (MTCT) is the primary route of human T‐lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV‐1) infection. Although formula feeding reduces breastfeeding‐associated transmission, MTCT still occurs, implicating pregnancy or delivery as key transmission windows. In this study, placental tissues from nine HTLV‐1–positive mothers were analyzed using DNA/RNAscope, revealing low HTLV‐1 DNA and RNA levels and a low RNA/DNA ratio, consistent with latent infection in the placenta and potentially explaining the low MTCT rate.

pmc-12500533.title: Deep Learning for Early Detection of Cardiovascular Diseases From Medical Imaging
pmc-12500533.creator: Sangeeta Davi, Mukesh Kumar, Zainab Muhammad Hanif, Ashvin Kumar, Muskan Kumari, F N U Ridham, Aiman Salam Shaikh, Insiya Fatima Azad, Manesh Kumar, F N U Suwasi, F N U Venjhraj, Amogh Verma
pmc-12500533.description: BackgroundCardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of mortality worldwide, making early detection vital for reducing morbidity and death rates. Echocardiography is a widely used, noninvasive imaging tool for diagnosing CVDs, but manual interpretation can be time‐consuming and subject to variability.

pmc-13226186.title: Key factors and serial mediation analysis of anxiety and depression among university students: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13226186.creator: Tan Jiang, Shijia Zhang, Deyou Jiang
pmc-13226186.description: BackgroundAnxiety and depressive symptoms are prevalent among university students; however, their risk factors are unlikely to operate in isolation. Instead, they may be organized in a multilevel structure that progressively approaches emotional outcomes, spanning from distal adversity exposure and the current family relational context, through resource pathways, to proximal functional status.

pmc-13396609.title: Durable response to pembrolizumab plus axitinib in platinum-resistant ovarian clear cell carcinoma: A case report
pmc-13396609.creator: Nikhil S Patel, Joshua J Cook, Danielle E Valcana, Michael J Poiesz, Shailesh J Patel
pmc-13396609.description: IntroductionOvarian clear cell carcinoma (OCCC) is a rare and aggressive histologic subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer characterized by intrinsic chemoresistance and limited treatment options in the platinum-resistant setting. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and VEGFR-targeted therapies have demonstrated synergistic activity across multiple malignancies, though their role in OCCC remains incompletely defined.

pmc-13679348.title: Evaluating COPD care assistance: a comparative study of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, and ERNIE bot performance
pmc-13679348.creator: Zhongshang Dai, Zihang Zeng, Zijie Zhan, Yan Chen
pmc-13679348.description: BackgroundLarge language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used to provide health information, yet their reliability in addressing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) care questions in the Chinese context remains unclear. To evaluate and compare the performance of three publicly available LLM chatbots – ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.
